title: Smugglers Built a Tunnel Under a Fake Store
central_question: Border fails: a cross-border tunnel came up under the storeroom floor of a fake discount store in San Diego (2026); smugglers zip-lined marijuana over the fence into Douglas, Arizona (2017); a tunnel from British Columbia ended under a living-room floor in Washington (2005). Which hideout was smarter?
content_notes: Tone: absurd and ironic; the joke is on the builds (a tunnel under a shop nobody shopped in, a zip line over the fence, a tunnel into a living room), never on a victim (none appears). Every case is a seizure by a named agency (a Homeland Security Task Force with San Diego County deputies; the US Border Patrol; US and Canadian agents with the U.S. Attorney in Seattle), a settled fact; the hook states the build. The four men charged in San Diego are charged, not convicted: never named and never drawn; prosecutors carry the freezer allegation ('Prosecutors say'). The man arrested in Douglas and the three men arrested in Lynden are never named and are drawn only as dark rim-lit silhouettes with no face (NOT A LIKENESS). Agents are generic figures in plain clothing with no badge, patch, flag, agency name or insignia; no weapon; no force shown; a torch only. The store, its signs, the freezer and the boxes carry no real company name, logo or livery (the store is shown as a plain 'SALE' shop, its real name only in the research ledger); the fence, the buildings, the hut and the house are generic illustrations, not replicas of the real places; the hidden-camera frame is our own typed graphic, not any real system's footage. Every card is our own typed graphic; no dialogue or quotation card. Facts verified 2026-10-25.

lines.text: Smugglers built a tunnel under a fake store.
Nearly 2,000 feet, all the way to Tijuana.
But agents noticed it had barely any customers.
In Arizona, smugglers zip-lined weed over the border.
Agents caught a man hiding in a vacant lot.
The strangest? A tunnel from Canada into a living room.
Agents had already hidden cameras inside.
Deputies found cocaine packed in freezers.

claims.text: A cross-border tunnel ran from Tijuana to a supposed retail store, 'Buy 4 Less', in Otay Mesa, San Diego, near the Otay Mesa Port of Entry; investigators say the store was a front. Charges announced 1-2 June 2026. Narration: 'Smugglers built a tunnel under a fake store.' Headline 'A TUNNEL UNDER / A FAKE STORE'. Label 'OTAY MESA, SAN DIEGO · MAY 2026'.

STATISTIC (counter 1,933 FT): the tunnel was about 1,933 feet long (prosecutors), about 55 feet deep and 4.5 feet high at points, into Tijuana; some outlets round it to 'nearly 2,000 feet'. Narration: 'Nearly 2,000 feet, all the way to Tijuana.' Counter '1,933 FT' with the label 'TUNNEL TO TIJUANA'.

The tunnel's exit was concealed under the floor of a storage room in the building; the store posed as a liquidated-goods retailer (appliances, luggage, household items). Label sub 'Exit under the storeroom floor'; illustration: boxed stock and suitcases on the shelves.

Homeland Security Task Force investigators watched the store from December 2025 to May 2026 after noticing suspicious activity: few customers but frequent movement by apparent employees, who moved apparently empty suitcases. Narration (gotcha): 'But agents noticed it had barely any customers.' Label 'ALMOST NO CUSTOMERS', sub 'Watched Dec 2025 - May 2026 (HSI)'.

The tunnel had its own hydraulic lift, electricity, ventilation and reinforced walls; reports also describe a rail system. The open hatch in the illustration is the lift's floor panel (drawn, not a reported image).

On 29 May 2026 deputies stopped three vehicles linked to the store and found 1,029.6 kg (2,269.87 lb) of cocaine, about $45 million; four men were charged (conspiracy to distribute; one also with tunnel and import counts). Charged, not convicted; none named or drawn. Label 'OVER A TON OF COCAINE · 4 CHARGED', sub 'Charged, not convicted (US Attorney)'.
Editorial rehook: the next case (a zip line over the border) is odder in kind than a tunnel. Narration: 'That was not the strangest.'

Wednesday 29 November 2017, Douglas, Arizona: Border Patrol agents seized more than 240 pounds of marijuana (10 bundles) sent across by a zip line fixed to a tall building in Agua Prieta, Sonora; Mexican authorities searched the line's origin and found no suspects. Narration: 'In Arizona, smugglers zip-lined weed over the border.' Label 'DOUGLAS, ARIZONA · NOV 2017', sub 'A zip line from a building in Agua Prieta'.

Agents using surveillance technology detected a person trying to hide in a vacant lot on the east side of Douglas; they found the bundles and an 18-year-old Douglas resident, who was taken into custody on drug smuggling charges. Not named; silhouette only. Narration (gotcha): 'Agents caught a man hiding in a vacant lot.' Label 'ARRESTED, 18 · NOT NAMED', sub 'Over 240 lb of marijuana (Border Patrol)'.

July 2005: a tunnel about 360 feet long ran from under a Quonset hut in Aldergrove, British Columbia, to beneath the living-room floor of a house on East Boundary Road in Lynden, Washington. Narration: 'The strangest? A tunnel from Canada into a living room.' Label 'LYNDEN, WASHINGTON · JULY 2005', sub 'About 360 ft, from a hut in British Columbia'.
FUN FACT: it was the first tunnel found under the US-Canada border (after many on the Mexican border). Card 'THE FIRST TUNNEL EVER / FOUND UNDER THE / US-CANADA BORDER'.

Tipped while the tunnel was being dug, US and Canadian agents monitored it; agents entered the Lynden house on a delayed-notice warrant and a federal judge authorised cameras and listening devices inside it; agents then watched three men make trips through the tunnel carrying large bags. Narration (gotcha): 'Agents had already hidden cameras inside.'

Three men from Surrey, BC, were arrested on 20 July 2005 and charged with conspiracy to import and distribute marijuana; agents seized about 42 kg (93 lb) of marijuana. Not named; silhouettes only. Label 'THREE MEN ARRESTED · JULY 2005', sub 'A judge approved the cameras (DOJ)'.

On 29 May 2026, prosecutors say, agents watched a van loaded at the store; three deep freezers were moved onto a truck and loaded with packages; San Diego County deputies stopped that truck (a K-9 alerted) and agents seized 173 packages from it, part of the 2,269.87 lb found in three vehicles. Narration (callback): 'Deputies found cocaine packed in freezers.' Inset card 'DEEP FREEZERS, PROSECUTORS SAY' (our own drawing of a generic chest freezer).
